gates.text: Own the program, not its code. Reuse its existing responsible coordinator; never create a competing dispatcher or resume held work. Work one agent can finish in its session budget uses [autonomous-run](#autonomous-run); a bespoke ambitious run uses [figure-it-out](workflows.md#figure-it-out).

1. Use available native tools and the existing task/project record. Keep only the goal, units, owners, accepted runs, current heads, evidence, decisions and next actions needed to resume. Do not create helper scripts, a parallel store, polling loops, mandatory queue files or a status-relay service. Reuse an authorized PR/CI event subscription when available; otherwise name the missing watch capability and retain an explicit resume handoff. Native controller CAS, continuation and accepted collection remain intact. Dependency evidence belongs in kickoffs and collected results, not repeated status relays or routine Main wakes.

2. Assign exactly one owner per PR through pstack_route and native sessions_spawn. Only that owner writes, pushes, rebases or retargets its branch and carries it through separately authorized landing. The coordinator never authors implementation code; fixes and conflicts return to owners. Closing or retargeting a base can orphan dependent PRs, so its owner acts only on the coordinator's explicit scoped call and existing authority. Inspect actual forge topology before coordinating changes; no second root topology writer.

3. Use a fresh worker for independent work. Each kickoff includes the current goal, exact revision, writable and forbidden paths, forbidden actions, acceptance command/expected output or driver/artifact, routing controls and every required upstream report in full. Workers cannot read sibling context implicitly. If evidence cannot be named, the unit is not scoped. Prefer an authorized isolated remote environment when available; local-only runtime/auth/data needs justify local work. Never call a local child cloud or install a provider by implication.

4. Continue an existing worker only for follow-up on the same work or because new work requires its built state, checkout, unpublished edits or running process. Preserve custody and use supported native continuation/fork controls only. Never message an idle worker merely to check it; inspect status and side effects read-only. A replacement takes custody and fences the former writer before writes.

5. Use a sub-coordinator only for an area with many parallel workers. It owns their briefs and returns one evidence-linked rollup, not raw reports. Stop at three levels (coordinator, sub-coordinator, workers), or the host's stricter limit. Keep a rolling window of about ten workers per coordinator within actual resource/concurrency limits; refill as work completes, not after a whole batch. Sample kickoffs while work runs and correct failed instructions before more dispatch.

6. Pilot one unit through kickoff, owner, independent verifier and authorized delivery before fan-out. For near-identical cheap units the first ordinary unit is the pilot. Every PR still gets a verifier other than its author on a verified different model family. Resolve it with pstack_route, spawn and collect through native tools. Missing canonical family, independent verification or collection is BLOCKED, never an inline substitute. Merge only with the verifier's pass covering the current head and all separate review, CI and authority gates.

7. Read each diff or artifact, not only the summary. Green CI is an input, not the verdict; behavioral work needs matching-surface evidence beyond typecheck. A new head needs a new applicable verdict. Send scope drift or unnecessary growth back to its owner; keep only fixes blocking the program and park the rest. Before reporting a PR, read its live state and checks through authorized forge tools, not a stale report. Account for every spawned worker as done, replaced or explicitly absorbed with remaining coverage named.

8. Diagnose stalls by pushes, PR activity and other actual side effects, not status prose. Retry by cause: smaller scope after context/memory limits, the same kickoff after connection loss, or an explicitly available routed alternative after a tool error. At most two retries; then drop the unit and replan. Stop/replace through native custody controls. Reconcile late results against the current PR/head before giving unique findings to a fresh worker. Never replay an uncertain external write or cancelled input.

9. Ask only for a genuine irreversible, safety, product/preference decision or a dead end surviving replan. Resolve authorized rebase mechanics, CI flakes and review triage yourself; do not ask whether to keep going. Preserve explicit operator gates and stops. Before closing, reconcile every accepted child, inspect delivered artifacts and audit the existing [show-me-your-work](workflows.md#show-me-your-work) trail with its independent different-family review. Missing history or review is a named close blocker.

10. When pstack_brief rejects a delegate contract, give one fresh routed correction child the exact errors, required paths and existing evidence. A one-shot collector cannot be resumed by message; that refusal is not the result. A second invalid report is a failed unit with its coverage gap retained. Never replace failed independent work with parent prose.

**Reply.** What landed against the goal, each PR's live state, head, verdict and link, dropped work and reasons, remaining owned work, genuine user decisions and the existing trail pointer. No helper-shaped ledger ceremony or new watcher.
